nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 1. Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a virus that usually causes symptoms similar to the common cold. It often causes upper respiratory infections but sometimes causes lower respiratory infections like pneumonia and asthma flare-ups or worsens chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text:
2. Symptoms include cough, runny or stuffy nose, fever, sore throat, wheezing or shortness of breath in severe cases. In some cases, the infection can escalate to bronchitis, pneumonia or asthma exacerbations.
credit : https://t.co/JiKfi5QgQT

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 3. Is HMPV life-threatening? It can result in bronchitis and pneumonia which is severe but young children, adults over 65, and susceptible individuals with underlying medical conditions or weak immune systems are at higher risk of severe illness or can lead to death. https://t.co/Fz92Ysm78Q

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 4. HMPV infection only lasts about 2-5 days and most people recover within about 7 to 10 days.

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 5. Is HMPV curable? Many healthcare providers can test and recognize the virus, but there is no established treatment for HMPV, and no vaccine is currently available for it. It is important to be cautious by wearing masks and applying sanitiser to reduce the risk of transmission. https://t.co/5SRZUCZxzf

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 6. can you get HMPV twice? Yes, it is one of the major pathogens of respiratory illness. Reinfection with HMPV occurs frequently throughout life.

nodes.author: UniPost69
nodes.text: 7. HMPV is highly contagious and has already become widespread in China. Recently, an eight-month-old baby in Bengaluru was diagnosed with HMPV. Similar to COVID-19, it has the potential to become another global pandemic if not effectively controlled. https://t.co/iNLDY2A9uW
